label: Palace
_model: Interior kernel at its most VANITY-shaped. A palace wants to be attended, delighted, admired or centred on, and its accommodations are what a court does to people who are useful to that.

appetites.purpose: nothing would ever have to be done alone

appeasement.move: do one small service without being asked, and well

appetites.want: never to be bored for an instant

appeasement.move: amuse it — a story, a trick, a scandal, anything new

appetites.want: to be surrounded by the finest of everything
appetites.purpose: nothing plain would ever be in the room

appeasement.move: admire something of its aloud and in detail

appetites.want: to be the reason everyone is in the room
appetites.purpose: every eye would always be on it

appeasement.move: give it your whole attention, and do not look away
appeasement.why: it is the centre of the room again

accommodations.text: retained {conscript} at court and would not sign their leave
ruined {conscript} so they could not afford to leave
commissioned {conscript} to work until the work killed them
favoured {conscript} so publicly that they could go nowhere else
had {conscript} dressed and posed about the rooms as furnishing
would not let {conscript} retire, and then could not

bell.label: the bell that was always answered
bell.function: the only thing the household ever obeyed instantly

mask.label: the mask from the last good revel
mask.function: the only night anybody remembers enjoying

jewel.label: the one perfect thing in a palace of fine things
jewel.function: the only object here that was never improved on

seal.label: the privy seal, still warm
seal.function: the only thing that ever ended a conversation

factions.name: the Household
factions.essence: still in service, still waiting to be rung for

factions.name: creditors
factions.essence: here for what the court still owes them

factions.name: the Court
factions.essence: still attending, still competing to be noticed

factions.name: what moved into the empty rooms

triggerGlossary.announced: came up the grand stair and were announced, as guests are
triggerGlossary.seenTwice: caught in two mirrors of the gallery at once
triggerGlossary.loud: a raised voice in a room built for conversation
triggerGlossary.lingering: stayed in one room long enough to be spoken about
triggerGlossary.disturbed: moved, sat on, or used something the household maintains

skirmish.avoid: they will not strike a guest who has been announced

fight.line: 1 Ghoul in the kitchens and 2 Skeletons

foes.name: Ghoul
foes.note: free Called Shot to freeze on a hit

fight.avoid: it stays below stairs; the state rooms are safe from it

battle.line: 1 Wraith of the Favourite and 3 Skeletons

foes.name: Wraith
foes.note: INCORPOREAL — chill touch ignores armour, drains 1 max Grit

battle.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the Skeletons
battle.avoid: it would far rather be flattered than fight, and will pause to be

nightmare.line: 1 Wraith, 1 Ogre in the under-stair and 4 Skeletons

foes.name: Ogre
foes.note: was the doorkeeper and still is

nightmare.harmedBy: blessed, silvered or magical weapons for the Wraith ONLY; anything for the rest
nightmare.avoid: do not run this without an appeasement route open

service.dangerLine: the household is still in service, and it is waiting to be rung for

institution: a bell-board with every room labelled and every wire taut
back-stairs running behind every wall so nobody is seen working
a servants' hall laid for forty
ritual: a tray carried up at the same hour to a room nobody is in
boots cleaned nightly and set outside doors
a bed turned down every evening
demand: a room where something is always just about to be handed to you
a chair drawn out before you reach it
a door that opens before you touch it
wound: a bell-wire pulled so hard it came out of the wall
a servants' hall with the table cleared in a hurry
livery folded and stacked by people who were leaving
anchor: a bell that was always answered, on its own hook
a book of household orders, current
a set of keys to every room, complete

features: a tray set down and not collected
boots cleaned and left outside a door
a bed turned down this evening
a bell still swinging on the board
livery laid out for tomorrow
a fire laid but not lit

decisions.cue: a bell-board with every wire taut and one still swinging
decisions.cost: answering it puts you in service; ringing it summons

resolve.success: you answer the bell and the Household takes you for staff — doors stop being locked
resolve.failure: you ring instead and something arrives expecting to be commanded
resolve.orElse: leave the board; the bell goes on swinging

decisions.cue: a tray carried up at the same hour to an empty room
decisions.cost: taking it up is service; eating it is presumption

resolve.success: you deliver it correctly and the Household will fetch and carry for you
resolve.failure: you eat from it and the court hears you were in the kitchens: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: let it go up as it always does; nothing changes

decisions.cue: back-stairs running behind the wall, unlit
decisions.cost: servants' passages go everywhere and nobody watches them

resolve.success: you navigate them and reach anywhere in the palace unseen
resolve.failure: you come out in the wrong room in front of the wrong thing
resolve.orElse: take the state rooms: seen, announced, one Turn

decisions.cue: a set of keys hanging where the housekeeper left them
decisions.cost: taking them is theft below stairs and authority above

resolve.success: you take them as though entitled and the Household hands you the rest
resolve.failure: you are caught taking them and are staff, not guests, from here
resolve.orElse: leave them; every locked door stays locked

decisions.cue: a fire laid but not lit in a room that is very cold
decisions.cost: lighting it announces occupancy

resolve.success: you light it and the room becomes yours — the Household attends you here
resolve.failure: the smoke draws something down the chimney: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it cold; you are not staying

decisions.cue: a book of household orders, current, in a fresh hand
decisions.cost: somebody is still writing the orders

resolve.success: you read who is issuing them and can countermand one
resolve.failure: you add an order and the Household carries it out too literally: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave it; the orders continue

situations.doing: carrying a tray up a stair to a room with nobody in it
situations.onArrival: they stand aside for you and wait
situations.because: the tray goes up at this hour and always has
situations.offer: take the tray up yourself and they will open anything you ask

situations.doing: counting linen that is already counted
situations.onArrival: it asks you, without looking, how many are staying
situations.because: the rooms must be made up for guests who never came
situations.offer: give it a number and rooms are made ready — and you are expected in them

situations.doing: swinging on the board with no hand on the wire
situations.onArrival: the label beneath it names a room above you
situations.because: somebody rang and nobody went
situations.offer: answer it and whatever is up there treats you as its own servant

situations.doing: going through a bureau, quietly, with a list
situations.onArrival: they look up and show you the list rather than hide it
situations.because: the court owes them and will not pay
situations.offer: help them find it and they will tell you which rooms are worth entering

situations.doing: holding a door open for somebody who is not coming
situations.onArrival: its arm does not lower
situations.because: it was told to hold the door
situations.offer: walk through and thank it, and it follows you and opens every other door

situations.doing: standing laid for forty with the food still warm
situations.onArrival: chairs scrape back very slightly
situations.because: the hall is laid at this hour and always has been
situations.offer: sit and eat and the whole Household counts you one of them

temptations.cue: a small bell from the board
temptations.benefit: ring it and one of the Household comes and does one thing
temptations.standingDrawback: the Household begins to expect instructions from you

temptations.cue: the housekeeper's keys, complete
temptations.benefit: one locked door per scene opens
temptations.standingDrawback: you are held responsible for what is behind them

temptations.cue: a suit of livery, pressed
temptations.benefit: the Household and the Court both ignore you
temptations.standingDrawback: you are given work, and it is noticed if undone

temptations.cue: the book of household orders
temptations.benefit: write an order and the Household obeys it exactly
temptations.standingDrawback: it obeys the letter of it, not what you meant

temptations.cue: a key to the servants' passages
temptations.benefit: move unseen between any two rooms, once
temptations.standingDrawback: something else uses the passages too, and now knows you do

delight.dangerLine: the court is bored, and boredom here has always been dangerous

institution: a card room with the tables still set mid-hand
a theatre built into a drawing room
swings hung from a painted ceiling
ritual: a revel begun and never formally ended
musicians' parts left open on stands, at the same bar
a wager entered in a book every evening
demand: a room that goes quiet when you enter, expectantly
a stage at one end of a salon, lit
a circle of chairs turned inward with one gap
wound: a masque costume torn off and left
a wager book with the last entries in a desperate hand
a theatre with the seats broken from inside
anchor: a mask from the last good revel

features: cards dealt for a hand nobody played
a mask dropped on a stair
a swing still moving
a wager written up this week
a musician's part turned to a new page
a costume laid out for somebody

decisions.cue: a room that goes quiet when you enter, waiting to be amused
decisions.cost: you are expected to be interesting

resolve.success: you amuse them and the Court adopts you — nothing here troubles a favourite
resolve.failure: you bore them and are dismissed: +1 Bane and the Court cuts you thereafter
resolve.orElse: leave quickly; you are talked about, and not well

decisions.cue: a hand of cards dealt and abandoned mid-play
decisions.cost: finishing the hand finishes something else

resolve.success: you play it out correctly and the Court is delighted — a door opens for the winner
resolve.failure: you play badly and owe the table: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the hand; it stays unfinished, which is worse for them than you

decisions.cue: a wager book with a space for a new entry
decisions.cost: the court will hold you to anything written

resolve.success: you enter a wager you can win and collect on it
resolve.failure: you enter one you cannot and are owed against for the rest of the delve
resolve.orElse: leave it; you are considered dull

decisions.cue: a stage at one end of a salon, lit, with nobody on it
decisions.cost: going up is an offer; walking past is a refusal

resolve.success: you perform something and the Court is yours for the delve
resolve.failure: you dry, publicly, and everything here saw it: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: walk past the stage; the lights follow you anyway

decisions.cue: a masque costume laid out in your size
decisions.cost: wearing it makes you part of the entertainment

resolve.success: you wear it and move through the palace as an expected part of the night
resolve.failure: you wear it and cannot take it off until the revel ends
resolve.orElse: leave it; you are conspicuous as yourselves

decisions.cue: an instrument still in tune in a room with no musician
decisions.cost: playing it restarts something

resolve.success: you play and the Court gathers, delighted, and will answer questions
resolve.failure: you play badly and something stops the music: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: leave it; the silence continues

situations.doing: holding a hand of cards that has not been played for centuries
situations.onArrival: one lays a card and looks up at you to follow
situations.because: the hand must be finished
situations.offer: play a card and they will pay you what the pot is worth

situations.doing: moving gently in a painted room with the windows shut
situations.onArrival: it slows as you come in
situations.because: the revel has not been ended
situations.offer: set it swinging again and the palace warms toward you

situations.doing: rehearsing an introduction for a guest who never arrived
situations.onArrival: it turns and begins introducing you instead
situations.because: the entertainment cannot begin without a guest of honour
situations.offer: let it finish and you are the guest of honour, with all that follows

situations.doing: stripping gilt off a theatre box, unhurriedly
situations.onArrival: they wave you in as though you were expected
situations.because: nobody has stopped them yet
situations.offer: join them and they will show you the room they have not dared enter

situations.doing: telling a story to a chair
situations.onArrival: it stops and asks whether you have heard this one
situations.because: the story has no ending and it cannot stop
situations.offer: supply an ending and it will tell you something true instead

situations.doing: sitting with their parts open at the same bar
situations.onArrival: the bar is played, once, badly
situations.because: the piece was never finished
situations.offer: finish the phrase and every door on the floor opens

temptations.cue: a mask from the last good revel
temptations.benefit: wear it and the Court takes you for one of its own
temptations.standingDrawback: you cannot be recognised by your own party while worn

temptations.cue: the wager book
temptations.benefit: once, make something happen by betting on it
temptations.standingDrawback: the book records what you owe if it does not

temptations.cue: a small instrument, in tune
temptations.benefit: once, gather everything nearby to listen
temptations.standingDrawback: they expect a second piece, and are critical

temptations.cue: a masque costume in your size
temptations.benefit: once, be whoever the costume is
temptations.standingDrawback: the Court holds you to that character

temptations.cue: a deck missing one card
temptations.benefit: once, know what somebody is about to do
temptations.standingDrawback: the missing card is somewhere, and matters

splendour.dangerLine: everything here was made to outshine something, and it is still competing

institution: workshops built into the palace so the makers never left
a gallery hung to a plan, each piece answering the last
an inventory listing every object and what it cost
ritual: a room redecorated each season, over the last one
gilding laid on gilding until the moulding is shapeless
a portrait repainted whenever the face displeased
demand: a plinth, empty, with a card still on it
an alcove cut for something that is not there
a frame hung with nothing in it, dusted
wound: a workshop with the tools laid down mid-cut
a ceiling half-painted and abandoned on the scaffold
a gallery where the finest piece has been taken and the gap not filled
anchor: one perfect thing in a palace of fine things
the inventory, complete and in one hand
a maker's mark on the underside of everything good

features: an empty plinth with the card still on it
gilding laid over older gilding
a portrait with the face repainted
an alcove cut for something absent
tools laid down mid-cut
a frame hung with nothing in it

decisions.cue: an empty plinth with the card still on it naming what stood here
decisions.cost: filling it means giving something of yours up

resolve.success: you set something of yours on it and the palace accepts the substitution — a door opens
resolve.failure: you set something worthless there and the palace notices: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the plinth bare; the gap keeps drawing things toward it

decisions.cue: an inventory listing every object here and what it cost
decisions.cost: reading it takes time; taking it takes more

resolve.success: you find which object is listed as beyond price and where it is kept
resolve.failure: you are still reading when something comes to check the count
resolve.orElse: leave it; you will not know what is worth taking

decisions.cue: a portrait whose face has been repainted more than once
decisions.cost: under the last face is the first one

resolve.success: you scrape it back to the true face and learn who this place belonged to
resolve.failure: you damage it and the Court will not receive you afterwards: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: leave the portrait; the face stays whatever it was last made

decisions.cue: a ceiling half-painted, scaffold still standing
decisions.cost: the scaffold reaches a floor no stair does

resolve.success: you climb it and reach the upper rooms without passing the state floor
resolve.failure: the scaffold gives and something below hears it: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: take the stairs; you pass through where you can be seen

decisions.cue: a gallery hung so each piece answers the last, with one gap
decisions.cost: the gap can be filled or admired

resolve.success: you admire the arrangement aloud, accurately, and the Court opens the next room to you
resolve.failure: you praise the wrong piece and are marked as no judge of anything
resolve.orElse: say nothing; you are handled as a tradesman thereafter

decisions.cue: a maker's mark on the underside of the best thing in the room
decisions.cost: the makers are still here somewhere

resolve.success: you match the mark to the workshop and can find the maker, who will help you
resolve.failure: you take the piece instead and the workshop knows immediately
resolve.orElse: leave it unread; the makers stay out of it

situations.doing: polishing a surface that is already finished
situations.onArrival: it moves aside and shows you the work rather than speaking
situations.because: the piece was never signed off
situations.offer: praise one specific thing about it and it will make you what you ask for

situations.doing: standing lit in a room where nothing else is
situations.onArrival: the light on it does not move when you do
situations.because: what stood here was taken and nothing replaced it
situations.offer: put something of value on it and the palace treats you as a benefactor

situations.doing: arguing silently over which of two vases is finer
situations.onArrival: they turn to you for a judgement
situations.because: the argument has run for centuries with no arbiter
situations.offer: choose one, confidently, and the loser's owner tells you what you want to know

situations.doing: measuring a frame with a length of string
situations.onArrival: they ask, without preamble, what you would pay
situations.because: the estate is being assessed and nobody has stopped them
situations.offer: name a price and they will tell you which room the good things are in

situations.doing: standing on a scaffold with a brush that has dried
situations.onArrival: it looks down and asks whether the light is right yet
situations.because: the ceiling was never finished and cannot be
situations.offer: tell it the light is right and it will come down and open the upper floor

situations.doing: hanging opposite another mirror in a narrow room
situations.onArrival: your reflection arrives a moment after you do
situations.because: the room was built to double everything in it
situations.offer: stand between them and be admired, and something in the depth of it answers a question

temptations.cue: one perfect thing, small enough to pocket
temptations.benefit: once, buy your way past anything that can be bought
temptations.standingDrawback: everything here recognises it as taken

temptations.cue: the inventory, complete
temptations.benefit: know the value and location of anything in the palace
temptations.standingDrawback: you know what you have not got

temptations.cue: a maker's punch
temptations.benefit: once, make a thing appear to be the finest of its kind
temptations.standingDrawback: the maker knows their mark has been used

temptations.cue: a hand-mirror in a heavy frame
temptations.benefit: once, see a room before you enter it
temptations.standingDrawback: what is in the room is also looking

temptations.cue: a leaf of gold from the workshop
temptations.benefit: once, make yourself look like somebody who belongs here
temptations.standingDrawback: it wears off at the worst moment

audience.dangerLine: the Court is still assembled, and it notices exactly who is being attended to

institution: a throne set so every sightline in the room ends on it
an order of precedence painted on the floor
a presence chamber with one door for entering and none for leaving
ritual: names read aloud at a door to nobody
a levée held each morning around an empty bed
backing out of a room that has nothing in it
demand: a chair at the centre and all the others turned toward it
a space kept clear that nobody will walk into
a silence that opens when you enter, waiting
wound: a throne room where the chairs have been turned outward
precedence scratched off the floor by somebody's heel
a door forced from the inside
anchor: a chair that nobody has ever been allowed to sit in

features: chairs turned to face one empty seat
precedence painted on the floor
a name read at a door
a space kept clear on the boards
a chair nobody sits in
a door held open from inside

decisions.cue: a throne set so every sightline in the room ends on it
decisions.cost: sitting is a claim; kneeling is a submission

resolve.success: you kneel correctly and the Court receives you — safe passage through the state rooms
resolve.failure: you sit, and every eye in the palace is on you from here on: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: stay standing; you are neither received nor refused, and doors stay shut

decisions.cue: an order of precedence painted on the floor with a gap at your rank
decisions.cost: standing in the gap accepts the rank

resolve.success: you take the correct place and the ceremony proceeds around you and past the guard
resolve.failure: you take too high a place and are challenged by something that outranks you
resolve.orElse: step off the pattern; you are escorted, not admitted

decisions.cue: a levée being held around a bed with nobody in it
decisions.cost: attending is required; leaving early is noticed

resolve.success: you attend it out and are afterwards owed a favour by everything present
resolve.failure: you leave in the middle and the Court cuts you: +1 Bane
resolve.orElse: do not go in; the door is shut behind you for good

decisions.cue: names being read at a door to nobody, and a pause
decisions.cost: giving a name gets you announced under it

resolve.success: you give a name grand enough to be believed and are announced and admitted
resolve.failure: the name is checked against the book and found absent
resolve.orElse: go in unannounced, and the Household treats you as staff

decisions.cue: a door that opens inward only, held by something on the other side
decisions.cost: it will open for the right form of words

resolve.success: you ask leave properly and it opens and stays open behind you
resolve.failure: you push, and it holds, and something takes note: roll the clock
resolve.orElse: find another way round, costing a Turn

decisions.cue: a chair at the centre with all the others turned toward it
decisions.cost: the room needs somebody in it

resolve.success: you put one of your own in it and the Court attends them — and ignores the rest of you
resolve.failure: the chair is taken by something else while you argue about it
resolve.orElse: leave it empty; the room stays restless and nothing here will settle

situations.doing: standing assembled and facing an empty chair
situations.onArrival: every head turns to the door as you come in
situations.because: the audience cannot begin and cannot be dismissed
situations.offer: take the chair, or seat one of your own in it, and be answered

situations.doing: reading names at a door to an empty corridor
situations.onArrival: it pauses, pen ready, and waits for yours
situations.because: the list must be got through
situations.offer: give a name and be announced, and be admitted wherever that name can go

situations.doing: waiting on a bench with a sealed letter and no patience
situations.onArrival: they ask how much longer, as though you would know
situations.because: they were told to wait and nobody came back
situations.offer: take the letter in for them and they will tell you the way out

situations.doing: sitting with its back to the room, quite still
situations.onArrival: the whole Court watches to see whether you approach
situations.because: nobody has been granted an audience in a very long time
situations.offer: approach properly and it will grant one thing, once

situations.doing: standing exactly on the line of its precedence
situations.onArrival: it will not move until somebody of higher rank passes
situations.because: the order must hold
situations.offer: outrank it, convincingly, and the corridor beyond opens

situations.doing: standing alone in the middle of a cleared floor
situations.onArrival: the boards around it are worn in a ring
situations.because: nobody has been allowed to sit in it and everybody has walked around it
situations.offer: sit, and everything in the palace comes to see who you are

temptations.cue: the privy seal, still warm
temptations.benefit: once, end any conversation on your terms
temptations.standingDrawback: what you sealed is now yours to answer for

temptations.cue: the book of precedence, current
temptations.benefit: know what outranks what, everywhere here
temptations.standingDrawback: you also know where you stand, and it is low

temptations.cue: a name from the usher's list
temptations.benefit: once, be announced as somebody with the run of the place
temptations.standingDrawback: somebody else answers to it and will find you

temptations.cue: a signet worn thin at the edge
temptations.benefit: once, be obeyed by anything still in service
temptations.standingDrawback: the Household reports to you, including things you would rather not hear

temptations.cue: a folding chair of state, light enough to carry
temptations.benefit: once, hold an audience anywhere
temptations.standingDrawback: whatever attends it is not always what you invited
